senses.gloss:
Gupta-kāśī
(‘hidden काशी’)
------------------------------------------
Situated at a distance of 34 kms. (21 miles) from रुद्रप्रयाग (in Uttaranchal) Guptakāśī is a small place of पिल्ग्रिमगे. Many sages of the olden days are said to have performed severe austerities here to realise Lord शिव. Bāṇāsura’s daughter Uṣā had her palace here.
There is a beautiful image of शिव as Ardhanārīśvara, riding his bull, the नन्दि, here.
In a pond nearby, two streams of water are constantly falling into it. These are called ‘Gaṅgā’ and ‘Yamunā’. Pilgrims take bath in this pond and give gifts secretly (gupta = secretly).

Gupta-godāvarī
(‘the hidden गोदावरी’)
------------------------------------------
Nearly 10 kms. (6 miles) from the अत्रि-अनसूया आश्रम in चित्रकूट (in Uttar Pradesh) there is a dark cave. About 15 metres (50 ft.) inside it, there is a pond called ‘Sītākuṇḍa’. Water streams constantly fall into this pond. Taking a bath here, is considered by the pilgrims, as equal to taking a bath in the sacred river गोदावरी. Hence the name ‘Gupta-गोदावरी’.

Gupta script
------------------------------------------
A modified form of the ब्राह्मी script, it has been used in the inscriptions of the kings of the Gupta empire during the period 4th to 6th centuries A. D. It had 37 letters including five vowels.
This script has been considered as the precursor of later Indian scripts as also of some Central Asian scripts.
See also BRĀHMĪ.
